coverage: Saturday 3 Oct 2026 ~07:02-07:50 SGT run, all markets closed for the weekend (next session Mon 5 Oct Asia open). One-session catch-up off Friday 2 Oct's US/HK/SG cash close (JP/KR bars read Thu 1 Oct per the price spine's latestByExchange) -- not a multi-day gap, since the last brief was Friday 2 Oct 07:45 SGT. The session Friday's tape was waiting on was September payrolls (released on schedule, no government shutdown in effect -- a 2 Sep stopgap funds the government through 11 Dec 2026): NFP crashed to +29,000 (vs ~84-90K consensus), unemployment rose to 4.2%, wage growth cooled to +0.1% m/m/+3.0% y/y (lowest since May 2021), and July/August were revised down a net -60K. Markets read it as 'bad news is good news' for the Fed -- Oct 27-28 hold odds surged to ~80-83%, the 10Y initially fell but still closed at a 24-year high above 5.3% on energy-driven inflation fear, and US equities rallied broadly (S&P +0.73% to 7,722.72, Nasdaq +1.19% to 27,190.86 on a fresh intraday record, Dow +0.49%, Russell +0.94%, VIX -6.59% to 15.31). That rally did NOT clean up the tape underneath it: Fear&Greed actually worsened to 28/Fear (from 31) as Safe-Haven and Junk-Bond-Demand components deteriorated and Strength/Breadth stayed pinned at extreme-fear 0, Friday-specific NYSE advance/decline and 52-week high/low counts could not be independently confirmed (two aggregators disagreed and may have mislabeled Thursday data as Friday's), and CCC-and-below credit spreads crossed the formal 1,007bps distressed threshold on 30 Sep -- the widest since the 2023 SVB collapse. HK tech took a second, distinct hit Friday: Hang Seng fell ~2.6-2.7% to ~23,950-23,970 (worst day since July) on the 24-year-high yield spike, a new US push to restrict Chinese data-center components, AND the loss of Stock Connect Southbound support (dark through 7 Oct for Golden Week) -- Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi all fell on the week. CityDev's standalone -14.8% weekly plunge was resolved: the Kwek family's 28 Sep announcement of a S$5bn China/Japan reinvestment plan paired with a S$6bn divestment drive, read by the market as a poor capital-allocation pivot rather than the net capital return investors wanted. tldr: September payrolls crashed to +29,000 (vs ~84-90K consensus) and unemployment rose to 4.2% -- Fed-hold odds for Oct 27-28 jumped to ~80-83% and stocks rallied hard (S&P +0.73%, Nasdaq +1.19% to a record, VIX -6.59%), but Fear&Greed actually worsened to 28/Fear and breadth stayed unconfirmed -- a genuine, not cosmetic, divergence under the rally.

The 10-year Treasury yield closed at a 24-year high above 5.3% despite the weak jobs print -- the real reason gold/silver popped on the miss then faded into the close (GLD -0.68%d, SLV -0.51%d) even as miners (GDX +1.20%d, SILJ +0.44%d) kept outperforming bullion.

HK tech sleeve took a second, distinct hit Friday: Hang Seng fell ~2.6-2.7% (worst day since July) on the yield spike, a new US push to restrict Chinese data-center components, AND the loss of Stock Connect Southbound support (dark through 7 Oct) -- Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi all down on the week.

CityDev's standalone -14.8% weekly plunge is resolved: a market backlash to the Kwek family's S$5bn China/Japan reinvestment plan paired with a S$6bn divestment drive, announced 28 Sep -- a company-specific capital-allocation story, not a broad SG-developer read-through.

Standing risk, unchanged this run: the levered silver sleeve sits -47.25% off its Jan 28 peak at 1.687x leverage vs a 1.4x target, stressed-call survivability FAIL, 25.9% from a margin call -- still the single biggest risk in the book.

Credit crack to watch: CCC-and-below spreads crossed the formal 1,007bps distressed threshold on 30 Sep, the widest since the 2023 SVB collapse, even as equities and broad high-yield stay calm -- an early-stage, narrow signal, not yet a broad one.

regime.label: Payrolls shock flips Fed to a near-certain October hold; broad Friday rally meets persistent CCC-credit and BOJ/MAS tightening cross-currents
regime.oneLiner: A brutal payrolls miss cemented an October Fed hold and sparked a broad equity rally, but credit cracks, an unconfirmed breadth recovery, and a 24-year-high in long yields keep this a two-sided, not a clean, risk-on regime.

topNews.headline: September payrolls crater to +29,000 (vs ~89k consensus), unemployment hits 4.2% -- stocks rally hard, Fed-hold odds jump to ~83% for Oct 27-28
topNews.actionable: This supersedes last night's preview and is the clearest signal yet that the Fed stays on hold rather than hikes or cuts this month, which is a mild net tailwind for the silver/miner sleeve and SGX banks' funding costs but not strong enough on its own to chase risk given the labor-market deterioration underneath the rally.

topNews.headline: 10-year Treasury yield hits a 24-year high above 5.3% on energy-driven inflation fear -- even the weak jobs print couldn't pull it down
topNews.actionable: A 24-year-high real-yield backdrop persisting despite a weak jobs print is the key tension behind Friday's gold/silver pullback into the close and is a genuine headwind for the cash pile's opportunity cost calculus and for SGX REITs' refinancing costs, even as it's a tailwind for DBS/OCBC/UOB net interest margins.

topNews.headline: Hang Seng plunges 2.7% to 23,943 (worst day since July) as Treasury yields spike and a new US ban on Chinese data-center gear hits tech; Stock Connect still dark until Oct 8
topNews.actionable: This is a second distinct headwind for the HK tech sleeve layered on top of the yield shock -- a widening US tech/data-center decoupling campaign -- and it happened on thin, mainland-free liquidity, so expect an amplified reaction (either relief or further selling) once Stock Connect flow returns October 8.

topNews.headline: CityDev (C09.SI) craters ~14.8% for the week -- investors punish Kwek family's S$5bn China/Japan reinvestment plan announced alongside a S$6bn divestment drive
topNews.actionable: This is a company-specific capital-allocation credibility problem (the market wanted net capital return, not a reinvestment pivot into China/Japan real estate) rather than a read on Singapore property broadly, so it argues against treating CityDev's drop as a signal to de-risk the SGX developer/REIT sleeve generally -- but it's a reminder to check whether other SGX developers announce similar reinvestment-heavy strategic reviews.

topNews.headline: Gold/silver spike on the jobs miss then fade into the close (GLD -0.72%d, SLV -0.02%d) as 24-year-high yields reassert themselves; miners outperform the metal again
topNews.actionable: The intraday pop-then-fade pattern confirms gold/silver are currently trading more off the real-yield/dollar axis than off Fed-cut hopes, so further payrolls-style misses won't sustainably lift the metals sleeve unless the 10-year yield itself breaks lower -- watch Treasury yields, not jobs data, as the next directional signal for the silver/miner positions.

signals: No research call clears the high-conviction bar this run (pUp3m >=0.6 or <=0.4 at confidence >=0.55) -- closest are SMH (pUp3m 0.59, confidence 0.50) and QQQ (pUp3m 0.57, confidence 0.55), consistent with a genuinely two-sided regime.

AMD: watch -- a fresh three-way convergence (congress buys, a 28-fund Q2 13F consensus, and WSB attention) lands right as AMD crosses a $1 trillion market cap, the newest addition to the signals roster.

Rare-earth basket: watch -- Lynas's -8.93% weekly drop is confirmed deal-dilution from its own Meteoric Resources acquisition, not a China-truce reversal (truce stays extended to 10 Jan 2027); USA Rare Earth got a new CEO and a fresh Jefferies Buy at $21.
